result.topic_en: Euler completes the solution for finding all squares a^2 such that a^2+1 is divisible by a given prime 4n+1=p^2+q^2, using a fraction r/s with ps-qr=±1, and begins a scholion on how to find such a fraction.
result.transcription:
106 DE NVMERIS PRIMIS
vnitate auctum per illum diuisibile sit $aa+1$. Demonstraui autem, quando summa duorum quadratorum, veluti $aa+bb$, diuisibilis est per numerum primum $pp+qq$, semper dari duos huiusmodi numeros $r$ et $s$, vt sit $a=pr+qs$ et $b=ps-qr$. Nostro casu ergo cum sit $bb=1$, necesse est, vt sit $ps-qr=\pm 1$: vnde perspicitur fractiones $\frac{p}{q}$ et $\frac{r}{s}$ proxime inter se convenire, ita vt earum differentia $\frac{ps-qr}{qs}$ minorem numeratorem, vnitati quippe aequalem, habere nequeat. Quare cum numeri $p$ et $q$ ex aequalitate $4n+1=pp+qq$ sint cogniti, formetur fractio $\frac{p}{q}$, quaeraturque in numeris minoribus fractio $\frac{r}{s}$ illi proxime aequalis, vt partibus per crucem multiplicatis productorum $ps$ et $qr$ differentia sit $=1$, id quod methodo a me alibi exposita facile fiet; tum ad fractionem $\frac{p}{q}$ inuenta hac fractione $\frac{r}{s}$, erit quadrati vnius quaesiti radix $a=pr+qs$, vel etiam $a=-pr-qs$. Tum vero si multiplum quodcunque diuisoris $4n+1$ addatur, habebitur quoque valor idoneus pro $a$. Generatim ergo erit $a=m(4n+1)\pm(pr+qs)$, in qua forma continentur radices omnium quadratorum, quae vnitate aucta per numerum primum propositum $4n+1$ sunt diuisibilia. Q. E. I.

Scholion.

Quemadmodum autem data fractione $\frac{p}{q}$ aliam fractionem $\frac{r}{s}$ inueniri conueniat, quae ab illa tam parum discrepet, vt producta per crucem orta $ps$ et $qr$ vnitate tantum differant, alio loco ostendi. Scilicet pro numeris $p$ et $q$ eadem operatio institui debet, quae
vulgo

items.quote: Demonstraui autem, quando summa duorum quadratorum, veluti $aa+bb$, diuisibilis est per numerum primum $pp+qq$, semper dari duos huiusmodi numeros $r$ et $s$, vt sit $a=pr+qs$ et $b=ps-qr$.
items.english: I have shown, moreover, that when a sum of two squares, such as aa+bb, is divisible by a prime number pp+qq, there always exist two numbers r and s such that a=pr+qs and b=ps-qr.

items.quote: Generatim ergo erit $a=m(4n+1)\pm(pr+qs)$, in qua forma continentur radices omnium quadratorum, quae vnitate aucta per numerum primum propositum $4n+1$ sunt diuisibilia. Q. E. I.
items.english: In general, therefore, a = m(4n+1) ± (pr+qs), a form containing the roots of all squares which, increased by one, are divisible by the given prime 4n+1. Which was to be found.

items.quote: Quemadmodum autem data fractione $\frac{p}{q}$ aliam fractionem $\frac{r}{s}$ inueniri conueniat, quae ab illa tam parum discrepet, vt producta per crucem orta $ps$ et $qr$ vnitate tantum differant, alio loco ostendi.
items.english: How, given a fraction p/q, one should find another fraction r/s differing so little from it that the cross products ps and qr differ only by one, I have shown elsewhere.
